scope_entries.surface: sibling repos: evidence-cli 0.6.1, rigor-cli 0.7.0, workledger-cli 0.8.0 (origin/main), coherence-cli 0.6.1
scope_entries.finding: evidence-cli and rigor-cli are template scaffolds with no domain code (evidence-cli pyproject.toml:4 promises grading, tree has only scaffold verbs; rigor-cli README.md:66-70 says the ledger is not implemented). workledger-cli has append/list with free-string refs and no verify verb. coherence-cli quality fidelity only detects that a quote exists and emits quote_accuracy_unverified (coherence/quality/heuristics.py:91). None reads an associate export, none grades an answer right or wrong, none scores a quote against a value. So neither the answer grader nor the per-fact score has an existing home outside associate.

scope_entries.surface: associate/accuracy/check.py, associate/cli/_commands/check.py, the run result (Python re-check)
scope_entries.finding: Python recomputes counts and verdicts from walk.jsonl, results and facts.json and never uses the extension's (check.py:894-896); the one value it copies is unchecked_text, labelled unchecked_text_source: extension (check.py:920-924), which is the pattern for a score it cannot recompute. The re-check is documented as standard library only, no model called (check.py:1-7). _check_fact builds each fact from a fixed set of keys (check.py:446-453), so a score in the saved files would be dropped unless copied on purpose. report.schema.json and the fact items of facts.schema.json forbid extra properties (report.schema.json:7, facts.schema.json:19). A missing optional field read with a guard is safe for old exports (check.py:855-860).

scope_entries.surface: associate/harness/pi.py and associate/cli/_commands/run.py (timeouts, reasoning, continue-from; issue #22)
scope_entries.finding: On --timeout the launcher kills pi and raises HarnessError (pi.py:844-851); _assemble_result is never reached (pi.py:760-770), so the caller gets exit 2 and no result object, though walk.jsonl and saved results stay in the export. Reasoning is per model in models.json and applied in lib/provider.ts:25-35,138-179; there is no per-run override (ASSOCIATE_REASONING only labels bench rows, bench/config.py:133). --continue-from loads the prior walk as context and labels it prior (pi.py:1033-1037, check.py:776-781); it is not a resume.

Six tasks, each with prompt, answer (free prose, 83 to 506 characters) and either evidence (file, line, text, stable) or absent (file, patterns); no structured expected values. Only tests/test_accuracy_tasks.py reads the file: it pins the path docs/accuracy/tasks.json (line 25), requires answer inside each task (line 67) and checks each evidence text against the file in the repo (lines 83-96). So the key cannot simply leave the tree or be split without changing that test.

scope_entries.surface: what a model can read: associate/contract/policy.json read.denylist, lib/contain.ts, tools/read.ts, tools/shell.ts, tools/search.ts, associate run --checkout, associate/harness/worktree.py
scope_entries.finding: policy.json has a read deny-list of secret-style globs (policy.json:9-32) applied by isDenylisted (contain.ts:390-411) from tools/read.ts:646 and tools/shell.ts:382 only; tools/search.ts has no deny or ignore logic, so grep and find are not covered. There is no per-run hide option. --checkout takes any existing directory (run.py:272-281); a writing model gets a git worktree at HEAD holding every tracked file (worktree.py:214-237), a read-only model runs in place (run.py:218-219). A filtered copy is therefore possible today only by hand, and only a git-tracked filtered clone keeps worktree isolation for writing models.

scope_entries.surface: associate/bench/ (suites.json, public.py, config.py, walkstats.py) and the 2026-10-27 multi-model spec
scope_entries.finding: associate bench runs public suites through their own upstream runner and scorer and never re-implements a scorer (public.py:5-6); every entry is verified: false. The in-house 7-case suite was dropped (CHANGELOG.md:416-417) under a recorded decision that every reported benchmark number comes from a public suite's own scorer (docs/specs/2026-10-27-associate-multi-model-on-pi-1-1-0.md:36-37, 231); the same spec notes nothing then benchmarks the harness itself (line 190). No grader exists that decides an answer right or wrong, and bench has no history store. A graded in-house comparison would reverse or narrow that earlier decision.

Every step was manual: a scratch clone, a hand-edited contract copy to turn reasoning off because there is no per-run switch (lines 17-20), 12 launches of associate run with --untrusted-checkout --timeout 1500 --json (lines 14-16), a hand count and a separate re-check script that is not committed (lines 65-72). Correctness of prose answers was not measured (line 198). A comparison with several arms and repeats needs a committed runner.
